Extraction.title: Extraction

LanguageProfile.description:
How we speak to and listen to one participant.

``stt_candidates`` maps to the Prisma v3.0 ``language_code`` list (1-4 codes); one code
forces the language, several act as a hint (docs.gnani.ai/api/STT/models/prisma-v3).
LanguageProfile.title: LanguageProfile

ParticipantPatch.description: Fields to change on a directory entry. The id never changes.
ParticipantPatch.title: ParticipantPatch

ParticipantSpec.description:
A participant registered on an investigation.

Display names are synthetic (programme rule: synthetic data only).
ParticipantSpec.title: ParticipantSpec

PresenceCheckView.description:
A presence check (docs/adr/0014). Nobody is accused: a failed check only means the
answer from that place counts for less, and someone else is asked.
PresenceCheckView.title: PresenceCheckView

RepairState.description: Belief about a repair that has been carried out.
RepairState.title: RepairState

ScenarioRequest.description: How the simulator should choose the sealed hidden fault.
ScenarioRequest.title: ScenarioRequest

SessionDevice.description: An opaque device reference, never the browser's session token.
SessionDevice.title: SessionDevice

StaffRole.description: What a signed-in person may do. Participants never sign in: they hold a signed link.
StaffRole.title: StaffRole

SubmitAnswer.description:
A participant's answer to the pending question.

Exactly one of ``text`` (free speech or typing, extracted into structured evidence) and
``outcome`` (a structured tap answer) must be given. ``participant_id`` must match the
participant the question was addressed to; it is never inferred from the text.
SubmitAnswer.title: SubmitAnswer

VoiceAnswerResult.description: A spoken answer: what Gnani heard, then the same result as a typed answer.
VoiceAnswerResult.title: VoiceAnswerResult

post.description:
Ask a human approver for a consequential action the decision calls for. The signed-in
account that asks is recorded; it cannot approve its own request.
The approved executor collects the single-use capability (expires in 5 minutes).

Needs the approver role. The approval records the signed-in approver; a free-text
``approver_id`` is used only when sign-in is not enforced (tests).

get.description:
The pending question, spoken in the participant's language (WAV).

Cached audio is one WAV. Otherwise the WAV is streamed while Timbre synthesises it
(``X-Audio-Streamed: true``; its header has an open-ended data length, as Timbre's own
WAVs do), so the browser can start playing before synthesis finishes.
Rebuild the investigation from its event log and compare with the recorded belief.

Push the investigation's events: backfill after ``after_seq`` (or the browser's
``Last-Event-ID``, whichever is later), then follow new events live.

200.description: Server-Sent Events. Each log event has `id: <seq>` and `data: <EventEnvelope>`. Control events: `ready`, `reset`, `bye`. Comments `: ping` are heartbeats.
